title: Saving Basics
content: Saving is the foundation of financial security. The 50-30-20 rule suggests allocating 50% of income to needs, 30% to wants, and 20% to savings. Start by building an emergency fund covering 6 months of expenses. Automate your savings by setting up automatic transfers on payday. Even small amounts compound over time - saving ₹5,000 monthly at 8% returns grows to ₹9.2 lakhs in 10 years.
keyTakeaway: Pay yourself first - save before you spend. Automate savings and build an emergency fund equal to 6 months of expenses.

title: Understanding Stocks
content: Stocks represent ownership in a company. When you buy a stock, you become a shareholder and can profit from the company's growth through capital appreciation and dividends. Stock prices fluctuate based on company performance, market sentiment, and economic conditions. Blue-chip stocks are shares of large, established companies with stable earnings. Growth stocks offer high potential returns but higher risk. Dividend stocks provide regular income. Diversification across sectors reduces risk.
keyTakeaway: Stocks offer ownership in companies. Diversify across sectors, invest for long-term (5+ years), and focus on fundamentals over short-term price movements.

title: Mutual Funds
content: Mutual funds pool money from multiple investors to invest in diversified portfolios of stocks, bonds, or other securities. Professional fund managers make investment decisions. Equity funds invest in stocks (higher risk, higher returns), debt funds invest in bonds (lower risk, stable returns), and hybrid funds mix both. Expense ratio is the annual fee charged - lower is better. NAV (Net Asset Value) is the per-unit price of the fund. Mutual funds offer instant diversification and professional management.
keyTakeaway: Mutual funds provide professional management and diversification. Choose funds based on your risk profile, check expense ratios, and invest through SIPs for rupee cost averaging.

title: Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs)
content: SIP is a disciplined way to invest fixed amounts regularly (monthly/quarterly) in mutual funds. It leverages rupee cost averaging - you buy more units when prices are low and fewer when high, averaging out the cost. SIPs remove the need to time the market. A ₹5,000 monthly SIP at 12% annual return grows to ₹11.6 lakhs in 10 years and ₹50 lakhs in 20 years. Start early to benefit from compounding. SIPs can be paused or stopped anytime, offering flexibility.
keyTakeaway: SIPs enable disciplined investing through rupee cost averaging. Start early, stay consistent, and let compounding work its magic over 10+ years.

title: Bonds & Fixed Deposits
content: Bonds are debt instruments where you lend money to governments or companies in exchange for regular interest payments. Government bonds (G-Secs) are safest with lower returns. Corporate bonds offer higher returns but carry credit risk - check ratings (AAA is safest). Fixed Deposits (FDs) are bank deposits with guaranteed returns and capital protection. FD interest is taxable. Senior citizens get 0.5% extra interest. FDs are ideal for short-term goals and emergency funds. Bonds and FDs provide stability to your portfolio.
keyTakeaway: Bonds and FDs offer stable, predictable returns with lower risk. Use them for capital preservation, emergency funds, and balancing equity exposure in your portfolio.

title: Index Funds
content: Index funds passively track a market index like Nifty 50 or Sensex. They invest in the same stocks in the same proportion as the index. Benefits include low expense ratios (0.1-0.5% vs 1-2% for active funds), no fund manager risk, and consistent market returns. Index funds are ideal for beginners and long-term investors. Nifty 50 has delivered ~12% annual returns over 20 years. They follow the philosophy that it's hard to consistently beat the market, so match it at low cost.
keyTakeaway: Index funds offer low-cost, diversified market exposure. Perfect for beginners and long-term wealth creation. Choose Nifty 50 or Sensex index funds for Indian market exposure.

title: Taxes & Section 80C
content: Section 80C allows tax deduction up to ₹1.5 lakhs annually on investments in PPF, ELSS, life insurance, NSC, and home loan principal. ELSS has the shortest lock-in (3 years) among 80C options. Section 80CCD(1B) offers additional ₹50,000 deduction for NPS. Long-term capital gains (LTCG) on equity above ₹1 lakh are taxed at 10%. Short-term gains are taxed at 15%. Debt fund gains are taxed as per your income slab. Tax-loss harvesting can offset gains. Plan investments to maximize tax benefits.
keyTakeaway: Use Section 80C (₹1.5L) and 80CCD(1B) (₹50K) to save taxes. ELSS offers best combination of tax saving and growth potential with 3-year lock-in.

title: Reading a Balance Sheet
content: A balance sheet shows a company's financial position at a point in time. Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Assets include cash, inventory, property. Liabilities are debts and obligations. Equity is shareholders' ownership. Key ratios: Debt-to-Equity (lower is better, <1 is good), Current Ratio (current assets/current liabilities, >1.5 is healthy), Return on Equity (net profit/equity, higher is better). Look for consistent revenue growth, improving profit margins, and manageable debt levels. Compare with industry peers.
keyTakeaway: Balance sheet reveals company health. Check debt-to-equity (<1), current ratio (>1.5), and ROE (>15%). Compare trends over 3-5 years and with competitors.

title: Diversification
content: Diversification means spreading investments across different asset classes, sectors, and geographies to reduce risk. Don't put all eggs in one basket. A balanced portfolio might include 60% equity (large-cap, mid-cap, small-cap), 30% debt (bonds, FDs), and 10% gold. Diversify within equity across sectors - IT, banking, pharma, FMCG. Consider international exposure through global funds. Rebalance annually to maintain target allocation. Diversification reduces volatility and protects against sector-specific downturns.
keyTakeaway: Diversify across asset classes (equity, debt, gold), sectors, and geographies. Rebalance annually. Diversification reduces risk without sacrificing long-term returns.
